Translate, as the Greek collocation of words, and the emphasis on "God" thrice repeated, requires, "For (in proof that "each shall receive reward according to his own labor," namely, from God) it is of God that we are the fellow workers (laboring with, but under, and belonging to Him as His servants, <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.20">2Co 5:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.6.1">6:1</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Acts.15.4">Ac 15:4</reference>; see on <reference osisRef="1Thess.3.2">1Th 3:2</reference>) of God that ye are the field (or tillage), of God that ye are the building" [Alford]. "Building" is a new image introduced here, as suited better than that of husbandry, to set forth the different kinds of teaching and their results, which he is now about to discuss. "To edify" or "build up" the Church of Christ is similarly used (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.21">Ep 2:21</reference>, 22; 4:29). <div eID="gen33072" type="x-p"/>

The "grace" is that "given" to him in common with all Christians (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.5">1Co 3:5</reference>), only proportioned to the work which God had for him to do [Alford].<div eID="gen33073" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33074" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wise--</hi>that is, skilful. His skill is shown in his laying a foundation. The unskilful builder lays none (<reference osisRef="Luke.6.49">Lu 6:49</reference>). How far wisely, and in builder-like style (<reference osisRef="1Pet.4.11">1Pe 4:11</reference>).<div eID="gen33076" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33077" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">buildeth thereupon--</hi>Here the building or superstructure raised on Christ the "foundation," laid by Paul (<reference osisRef="1Cor.2.2">1Co 2:2</reference>) is not, as in <reference osisRef="Eph.2.20">Ep 2:20</reference>, 21, the Christian Church made up of believers, the "lively stones" (<reference osisRef="1Pet.2.5">1Pe 2:5</reference>), but the doctrinal and practical teaching which the teachers who succeeded Paul, superadded to his first teaching; not that they taught what was false, but their teaching was subtle and speculative reasoning, rather than solid and simple truth. <div eID="gen33077" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 10. grace ... given unto me-- Paul puts this first, to guard against seeming to want humility, in pronouncing himself "a WISE master builder," in the clause following [Chrysostom]. The "grace" is that "given" to him in common with all Christians ( 1Co 3:5 ), only proportioned to the work which God had for him to do [Alford]. wise-- that is, skilful. His skill is shown in his laying a foundation. The unskilful builder lays none ( Lu 6:49 ). Christ is the foundation ( 1Co 3:11 ). another-- who ever comes after me. He does not name Apollos; for he speaks generally of all successors, whoever they be. If any ... defile ... destroy--</hi>rather as the Greek verb is the same in both cases, "destroy ... destroy." God repays in kind by a righteous retaliation. The destroyer shall himself be destroyed. As temporal death was the penalty of marring the material temple (<reference osisRef="Lev.16.2">Le 16:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.5.2">Da 5:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.3.30">3, 30</reference>), so eternal death is the penalty of marring the spiritual temple--the Church. The destroyers here (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.16">1Co 3:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.17">17</reference>), are distinct from the unwise or unskilful builders (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.12">1Co 3:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.15">15</reference>); the latter held fast the "foundation" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.11">1Co 3:11</reference>), and, therefore, though they lose their work of superstructure and the special reward, yet they are themselves saved; the destroyers, on the contrary, assailed with false teaching the foundation, and so subvert the temple itself, and shall therefore be destroyed. (See on <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.10">1Co 3:10</reference>), [Estius and Neander].
